crossRefs.note: so am I made to possess months of misery, wearisome nights are appointed to me.
When I lie down, I say, ‘When will I arise, and the night be gone?’ I toss and turn until the dawning of the day.
If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad face, and cheer up;’
I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that you will not hold me innocent.
I am weary with my groaning. Every night I flood my bed. I drench my couch with my tears.
You hold my eyelids open. I am so troubled that I can’t speak.

translations.web: When I say, ‘My bed will comfort me. My couch will ease my complaint;’
translations.bsb: When I think my bed will comfort me and my couch will ease my complaint,
